title: Machine Learning in Practice
description: Data preparation, experiment design, deployment, and monitoring essentials.

questions.prompt: Why define a feature schema for a production model?
options: To specify expected names, types, and constraints
questions.explanation: A schema lets systems catch malformed or incompatible inputs before they silently affect predictions.

questions.prompt: Train-serving skew occurs when training-time and prediction-time data processing differ.
questions.explanation: Different transformations or feature definitions can make production inputs unlike what the model learned.

questions.prompt: Where should a learned imputation value be fit in a train-validation pipeline?
options: On the entire dataset before splitting
questions.explanation: Fitting preprocessing on training data prevents information from validation or test partitions leaking into the pipeline.

questions.prompt: Which are useful input-data quality checks?
options: Check category values against allowed sets
Assume schema-valid data is always accurate
questions.explanation: Schema and distribution checks catch many defects, though they cannot prove values are semantically correct.

questions.prompt: What is concept drift?
options: A change over time in the relationship between inputs and the target
A change in a model’s source-code license
questions.explanation: Concept drift concerns changes in P(target|input); it differs from input-only distribution changes.

questions.prompt: Production model quality can be difficult to measure immediately when ground-truth labels arrive late.
questions.explanation: Delayed outcomes require proxy monitoring or waiting for labels before calculating direct quality metrics.

questions.prompt: What is a canary model deployment?
options: Route a limited amount of traffic to a new version before wider rollout
Train the model on one class only
questions.explanation: A canary limits exposure while operators compare behavior and detect regressions before full release.

questions.prompt: What supports a safe model rollback?
options: Overwrite the previous model without record
questions.explanation: A reproducible prior version and explicit criteria enable recovery if a new release causes problems.

questions.prompt: What is batch inference?
options: Scoring a collection of examples in a scheduled or grouped job
Updating model weights after each user click
questions.explanation: Batch inference processes many inputs together, often when immediate per-request results are unnecessary.

questions.prompt: When is online inference especially appropriate?
options: A prediction is needed promptly for an individual request
All predictions can wait for a nightly job
The model has no input features
The dataset is stored offline only
questions.explanation: Online inference serves predictions with low latency during an interactive or real-time workflow.

questions.prompt: Model versioning should include enough metadata to connect an artifact to its training data and configuration.
questions.explanation: Lineage helps reproduce, audit, and compare model versions.

questions.prompt: Why should feature-importance rankings be interpreted cautiously?
options: They may be model- and data-dependent and do not prove causation
They eliminate the need for validation
questions.explanation: Importance measures describe associations under a method’s assumptions; they are not automatically causal explanations.

questions.prompt: After detecting input drift, what are sensible actions?
options: Investigate the affected feature and population
Evaluate performance when labels become available
questions.explanation: Drift merits diagnosis and performance checks; automatic retraining without understanding can amplify problems.

questions.prompt: What is data minimization?
options: Collect and retain only data needed for a defined purpose
Remove the target column from all datasets
questions.explanation: Minimization reduces exposure by limiting personal data to what the task requires.

questions.prompt: There is one fairness metric that is appropriate for every model and decision context.
questions.explanation: Fairness criteria can conflict and depend on context, affected groups, and consequences.

questions.prompt: What is a shadow deployment often used for?
options: Run a candidate model on live inputs without using its outputs for decisions
Allow a model to rewrite its own source code
questions.explanation: Shadow mode gathers real-input behavior for comparison while keeping the existing decision path in control.

questions.prompt: Which belong in a model incident response plan?
options: A way to disable or fall back from the model
A promise that incidents cannot happen
questions.explanation: Operational plans need recovery options, clear ownership, and evidence for investigation.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a data contract between a producer and model service?
options: Make expectations about fields and changes explicit
Guarantee that the model is unbiased
questions.explanation: Contracts coordinate schema and compatibility expectations between systems exchanging model inputs.

questions.prompt: A calendar schedule alone is always sufficient to decide when a deployed model should be retrained.
questions.explanation: Retraining may depend on drift, label evidence, business changes, and evaluation—not merely elapsed time.

questions.prompt: What information is useful in a model card?
options: Intended uses, evaluation context, limitations, and known risks
questions.explanation: A model card communicates scope and evidence so users can judge where a model may be suitable.
